# WO-238 — A document says what is so: every committed document is standing, record or generated by a derived kind, a standing document has a reader and holds current state, session-start reads name standing documents only, a read census from the journals red-tags what no entry point names and no session reads, the reducer gets a lens that sees documents, a proposal learns what shipped it, and the kit's templates, the index cards, the planning root and the execution guide follow the contract (v0.113.0)

Until now nothing in the kit said what kind of document a file was or who read it. The fork's operator record had grown to 34 KB and its repository profile to 32 KB under a `Checked:` field that narrated nineteen orders, core's execution guide carried 133 dates and a chain of "one more screen" paragraphs, 51 dated pass documents stood beside the planning sequence and map, the only signal the document check gave was bytes against a ceiling, and twelve proposal packets had shipped without a field saying which order carried them. The operator's direction of 2026-10-28 was that usefulness, not bytes, decides, and that a document nobody uses goes.

This change gives every committed document one of three kinds, derived from its path with a short override list in `docs/control/documents.json` and the paths the kit's own commands write built in: a standing document states what is so for its reader and is replaced in place, a record is dated and never rewritten, a generated page changes only through its command. A standing document's reader binding is derived too, from the four reader entry points (the root instruction file's Start here, the skills' `Read:` lines, the execution guide's cold-start order and the kit guide's First steps), the links that reach it through standing and generated pages, and the programs that read it by its literal path. `npm run test:docs` now refuses an entry point that names a record and a red tag a planning pass left undisposed, reports each standing document no reader reaches, and judges no document's bytes: the ceiling file and its check are gone.

`npm run plan -- documents` adds the read census: from the session journals the hooks already write, this checkout's, the retained lanes of closed orders and the registered main checkout's, it counts the sessions that read each document over the last five releases, labels Codex unobserved, and lists the records an entry point names, the unbound documents a session still reads, the bound ones nobody read and the red tags: standing documents no reader reaches and no session read. `plan start` writes those tags into the new pass document's red-tag block, which names the pass whose block it follows, and the next pass removes or folds each with a disposition the check requires. Nothing removes a document by itself. The first census on this checkout red-tagged 27 documents, recorded in the decisions, and this order removed none.

The dated planning documents, 51 of them with the retired map copy and the release-history notes, moved under `docs/planning/passes/` by `git mv` and keep their bytes; `docs/control/document-moves.json` says where each went, and every reader of a document reference, the link check, the entry points, the bindings, the red tags, the census, `plan documents` and the kit export, resolves an old path through that one map, so a reference names one document for all of them and a moved path is never reused. `docs/planning/README.md` names what a pass reads and leaves. Product 07 is split by reader on a census of its sections: every heading stays, the operator's own procedures move to `docs/product/operator-reference.md`, five dated accounts move to `docs/planning/passes/execution-guide-record.md`, and 46 dated bracket citations become links to their records.

A filed proposal packet now carries `deliveredBy`: `npm run entropy -- dispose <REVIEW-NNN> <packet-id> route '<reason>' --order WO-NNN` names the order, release preparation names the release in the order's own change, and release close refuses to publish while a packet routed to the closing order names none, printing the route command that completes it from a planning branch of main; the twelve packets are backfilled from the release tags. The Entropy Reducer gains a fifth lens, `documents-and-readers`. The kit's repository-profile template replaces `Checked:` with `Current at:` and one rule, the workstream template gains a Rules section that holds rules while the member orders hold the history, the instance's root instruction file names the three kinds in one sentence, the index card drops its Cost paragraph while the order keeps the field, and the shared instruction's residue is one line per profile, so core's `CLAUDE.md` block fell from eleven lines to three.

The verification sequence is two reports. VER-001 failed on two blocking findings: a Start here link through the move map reached a record that the entry-point check and `plan documents` omitted, and a packet routed after its order's last preparation kept no release after a close; the repair gave every reader one reference resolution and made the close refuse before publication, and VER-002 passed with one follow-up: a moved record's relative links resolve through the map and not in an ordinary Markdown renderer, which the decisions board for the operator and planning. The final review integrated WO-252 from main, resolved one oracle collision with a two-parent integration oracle, retimed the skeleton package to 0.81.0 and the release to v0.113.0, and ran the complete review gate once at the integrated code identity; it passed, and the document gate passed on the candidate tree. The report is [FINAL-001](FINAL-001.md); the decisions are in [decisions.md](../../evidence/WO-238/decisions.md); the release notes are [RELEASE-NOTES.md](RELEASE-NOTES.md).

Limits a reviewer should know: the census is a lower bound, because Codex tool calls are unhooked; a program binding is a textual match of a literal path, so a document a command reads through a path it assembles at run time is reported unbound; and the executor, verifier, planner and release-close role roots exceed their effective cold-start ceilings on the integrated tree, measured and boarded as FUP-916e24773df0b734 for a planning allocation under product 07's one route, with no ceiling raised.
